title: Furifont, a Japanese font that shows furigana
content:
Comments

shun_dev · Oct 17, 2026

Really nice font! Native Japanese speaker here, and seeing furigana done purely in the font is very cool.

One small thing on the Japanese version of the page: in the "Ligatures do the work" section, 合字 itself only gets じ over 字, and 合 has no reading. It should be ごうじ. I guess 合字 isn't in the dictionary, so it falls back to single kanji, and 合 is skipped because it has several readings.

jbm · Oct 17, 2026

This is an interesting use of ligatures for sure. However, I really don't know when one would use it. Couldn't you just use Ruby tags for a website?

guipsp · Oct 17, 2026

Why do something manually when it can be done automatically?

yorwba · Oct 17, 2026

When you control the content, I agree that ruby tags would be better, since they can easily handle alternative readings and also enable smarter automation to infer the correct reading from context.

But you could set this as the default system font for Japanese and enjoy furigana everywhere, even in places that don't support ruby tags at all.

That’s incredible. I’m always impressed with the utility of the TrueType/open font spec - the flexibility there is really an underappreciated work of engineering genius.
